long_biography.plain_text:
Building SoFi Stadium around the relocated Los Angeles Rams shows how Stan Kroenke combines professional sport with property development. The privately financed venue anchors a wider district of shops, homes, offices and hotels, extending a model in which his holding company owns teams, arenas and media outlets.

That appetite for ownership developed early in rural Missouri. Kroenke worked long summer days in his father's lumberyard, kept its books and, while at university, borrowed $1,500 from his father at interest to buy into a clothing shop. After building real estate partnerships, he began acquiring teams and assembled a portfolio spanning American football, basketball, ice hockey and English football.
